clue.text: Officer giving advice to colleagues

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
one's staff are the people one works alongside

explanation.surface: A senior official hands out advice to the people working under them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, originally one carrying a metal-tipped staff of office.

clue.text: Before knight arises, touch The Flower of Baghdad

indicators.note: the touch word comes before the knight in the answer

parts.note: tig is the playground chasing game where you touch someone to make them 'it'

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the knight's title is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A chivalric ceremony: a knight stands up after a touch of the sword, with some exotic bloom of Baghdad mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' reverses SIR to RIS, read upward in this down light. 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river, a thing that flows; TIG is the British name for the game of tag.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris is the river running through Baghdad, and a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Home for Rick Stein's two packs

parts.note: to pad is to pack with stuffing, and to stow is to pack away: two verbs for packing
to pad is to pack with stuffing, and to stow is to pack away: two verbs for packing

explanation.surface: The TV chef Rick Stein's house is described by what he packs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rick Stein is a British TV chef whose restaurants are in a small Cornish fishing port.
explanation.definitionFit: The celebrity chef Rick Stein made his name with a seafood restaurant in this Cornish harbour town.

clue.text: Refresher course might be part of it

definitions.meaning: a refresher is a reviving drink, such as a cuppa

definitions.text: course might be part of it
definitions.meaning: a meal in the late afternoon, where a course of sandwiches or cake is one part

explanation.surface: A training refresher course might form part of some programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refresher course' looks like retraining; it is a refreshing drink, and also an afternoon meal that can have courses.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is the classic British refresher, and the afternoon meal of the same name can have courses.

clue.text: Attention seekers having a flutter? Not really

definitions.text: Attention seekers having a flutter? Not really

parts.words: Attention seekers having a flutter? Not really
parts.note: things worn to catch the eye that flutter on the eyelid, yet are not genuine, hence 'not really'

explanation.surface: Show-offs placing a bet, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a flutter' suggests gambling, a British idiom for a small bet; here it is the fluttering of lashes, and 'Not really' says they are fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-on fake lashes are worn to draw admiring looks and are fluttered flirtatiously.

clue.text: The last turn in game wasted, Karpov and his winning chances disappeared?

definitions.text: Karpov and his winning chances disappeared?

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: the turn letter goes inside the word game
wasted means ruined, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn gives the letter U

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: Karpov's final move was squandered, and he and his hopes of victory vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside GAME, and 'wasted' rearranges GAUME into EUGMA. The definition is an example: one verb, 'disappeared', governs Karpov literally and his chances figuratively.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeugma is a figure of speech where one verb serves two nouns in different senses, as here.

clue.text: Provoked in Exeter cab rank one day

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the rearranged letters
rank means foul or gone bad, so the letters of the two words are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: A is a word for one

explanation.surface: Someone was riled at the taxi rank in Exeter, a Devon city, one day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' rearranges EXETERCAB, and 'in' (placed first) puts A for 'one' inside that, making EXACERBATE before D. 'Cab rank' reads as a taxi stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To exacerbate can mean to irritate or anger someone, a secondary sense beside making worse.

clue.text: On beck, stab a thug

indicators.note: in this down clue the stab word sits on top of the stream word

parts.note: a stab at something is a go, an attempt
a beck is a northern English stream, and a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A heavy at someone's beck and call lashes out with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beck' suggests 'at someone's beck and call'; it is the northern English word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is slang for a big, brutish heavy or hired muscle.

clue.text: Young singer needing assistance to enter Commonwealth city

indicators.note: the help word goes into the singer's name

parts.note: Adele is a singer who found fame young, with albums named after her ages
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A youthful vocalist needs help getting into a city of the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia, an Australian city in the Commonwealth.

clue.text: Crack construction worker shows up on site

definitions.text: Crack construction worker shows up on site

parts.words: Crack construction worker shows up on site
parts.note: the cleavage a labourer reveals above low-slung trousers while working at a building site

explanation.surface: An expert builder appears at the building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective meaning expert; it is the noun, the cleft displayed when a workman's trousers slip, a British joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for the bare bum-cleft shown by a bending tradesman.

clue.text: Snout's part nuzzling bill opened by German duck

indicators.note: the bill word has the German letter at its start
nuzzling means pressing close, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: an ad, or advert, is a bill posted up
in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snout the tinker plays the part of Wall

explanation.surface: An animal's snout nuzzles a beak, with something German about the duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snout' looks like a nose; it is Tom Snout in Shakespeare's play, who acts the Wall in the mechanicals' play.
explanation.definitionFit: The gadwall is a greyish dabbling duck of Europe and North America.

clue.text: American in need of assistance from newsgroup at re-election

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A US voter seeks help from an online discussion group during an election campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Up a tree is chiefly American slang for being stuck in a difficult situation.

clue.text: Heading for unknown hotel in Tube disruption

indicators.note: a disruption throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone heading for a hotel is caught up in disruption on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into the blue is to set off into the unknown without a plan.

clue.text: Emperor's order to cut short animated ladies?

indicators.note: the emperor and order letters cut into the middle of the rearranged letters
animated means lively, so the letters of short are stirred about

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An emperor commands that some cartoon women be trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges SHORT to THROS, and 'to cut' places NEROOM inside it, between THRO and S. The definition plays on 'throne' as slang for a toilet, so ladies' loos.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is a name for women's toilets, and a throne is jocular slang for a lavatory seat.

clue.text: 'Arable area' covers it

indicators.note: the quoted words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A phrase that includes the thing in question within its scope.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'arabLE Area', and is itself arable land, so the whole clue both builds and defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is an old word for open grassland or meadow, often ploughed and sown.

clue.text: Letters to press question Yorkshireman, confined to a bed sick with worry

indicators.note: the Yorkshireman is shut inside the rearranged letters
sick means unwell, so the letters of a bed and worry are disordered

parts.note: tyke is a nickname for someone from Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A worried man from Yorkshire, bedridden, gets a letter for the press asking him questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges ABEDWORRY into WERYBOARD, and 'confined to' puts TYKE inside it after WER. Tyke is a British nickname for a Yorkshireman.
explanation.definitionFit: The keys of a standard typing layout are letters that one presses.

clue.text: Keeping yellow liquid in organ as ultimately you've neglected heart

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the organ word

parts.note: the ear is an organ

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of as
the middle letter of you've is left out

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A medical note: a yellowish fluid builds up inside some organ because the heart has been neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives S, 'neglected heart' takes U from YOUVE to leave YOVE, and 'in' puts SYOVE inside EAR. The definition describes an egg fried on both sides with a runny yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked this way is flipped briefly so the yolk stays runny and liquid.

clue.text: Ask for cryptic reading that will ultimately prove unrewarding

parts.note: the word ask is made by putting A before task with TA, slang for thanks, taken away

explanation.surface: A request to interpret a puzzle's wordplay that will in the end prove fruitless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cryptic reading' tells you the answer, read cryptically, makes the clue's word: A plus TASK lacking TA (British slang for thanks) gives ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: A job that earns no gratitude or reward is described by this common phrase.

clue.text: Droning sounds of uncertain diagnosis doctor's emitting after entry to hospital

indicators.note: the remaining letters come after the hospital's opening letter
the opening letter of hospital
the doctor is placed between the two hesitant noises he gives out

parts.note: um is the noise of hesitation, given twice for the plural sounds
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's hesitant murmuring as a patient is admitted makes for a dreary noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitting' sets DR between UM and UM, after H from 'entry to hospital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull and monotonous, like a droning, tedious voice.

clue.text: Soldier detected in secure state capital

indicators.note: the soldier word is found inside the word for secure

parts.note: safe means secure
a soldier ant is a caste of ant, so soldier gives ant

explanation.surface: A soldier is discovered inside a secure place in a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of the US state of New Mexico.

clue.text: Japanese flier wearing jacket

parts.note: erk is RAF slang for a lowly aircraftman
to be in a garment is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A Japanese pilot dressed in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: ERK is old British forces slang for the lowest rank of airman.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Tuber might, on journey back

indicators.note: travelling back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: may and might are both verbs of possibility

explanation.surface: A root vegetable could, perhaps, make a return trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The yam is a starchy tropical tuber eaten like a potato.

clue.text: Agreement on square: pimp closes place of vice

parts.note: re means on, concerning
S is short for square in addresses

indicators.note: the pimp word closes round the place of vice, enclosing it

parts.note: ponce is British slang for a pimp
a den is a place of vice, as in den of iniquity

explanation.surface: A deal is struck in a town square where a pimp shuts down a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: PONCE is British slang for a pimp.
explanation.definitionFit: Respondence is an archaic word for correspondence or accord, a matching between things.

clue.text: Observe orders not given to Trappist ways

indicators.note: orders here is a verb meaning arranges, so the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Religious orders, such as the Trappists, keep observances other monks do not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' suggests monastic orders, fitting 'Trappist', but it is the anagram signal. Trappist monks are known for keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks keep near-silence, so someone wordy and talkative is the opposite.

clue.text: Help to improve the outlook as president returns in an instant

indicators.note: the turned name goes inside the word for an instant

parts.note: in a tick means in an instant

indicators.note: returns means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A president comes back and instantly lifts everyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ABE into EBA, and 'in' puts it inside TICK. 'Outlook' looks like optimism; it is the view from a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A tieback holds a curtain open to the side, improving the view out of the window.

clue.text: This, or the openings to 1A and 5?

definitions.text: This, or the openings to 1A and 5?

parts.words: This, or the openings to 1A and 5?
parts.note: it is the final clue, and the starts of the two answers named both mean the extreme point of something

explanation.surface: A puzzling self-reference to how two other entries begin.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the last clue, so it is literally the finish. TIPSTAFF opens with TIP, and ZEUGMA opens with Z, the last letter; both are words for the extremity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is the extremity of something and Z is the final letter, so both are a finish.

clue.text: Lax teacher's about to get sent to Head

indicators.note: the word for about is put at the front, at the head

parts.note: re means about, concerning
miss is a schoolchild's name for a female teacher

explanation.surface: A careless teacher is about to be sent to see the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to Head' looks like a school punishment; it moves RE to the front of MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means careless or negligent in one's duty.

clue.text: A little fly squashed by a little man

indicators.note: the fly is pressed inside the word for a little man

parts.note: a son is a little man, a boy
a midge is a tiny fly

explanation.surface: A small insect is swatted by a short fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, a variant of smidgen.
